# Approach for posterior predictive checks
The goal of posterior predictive checks it whether the fitted models reproduce statistical features of the observed data. Therefore we use our posterior draws of engine ratings and other parameters like draw tendency to produce new tournament data and calculate the same summary statistics for the actual tournament and for each replicate.

We plot the observed statistics alongside their posterior predictive distributions and use this to guide a revision if needed. We then repeat the checks and record what changed, why, and whether the revision improved the fit.

## Model without time control

### Load Data

```{r}
# Load dataset
games <- read.csv("../../../data/games.csv")

# Basic characteristics
str(games)
cat("Missing values:" , sum(is.na(games)))
```

### Data Preparation for Stan

```{r}
engines <- sort(unique(c(games$white, games$black)))

# Encode outcomes:
# 1 = White win, 2 = Draw, 3 = Black win
outcome_levels <- c("1-0", "1/2-1/2", "0-1")

stan_data <- list(
  N = nrow(games),
  K = length(engines),
  white = match(games$white, engines),
  black = match(games$black, engines),
  outcome = match(games$result, outcome_levels)
)

table(stan_data$outcome)
```

### Posterior Sampling

```{r}
stan_file <- "helpers/rating_three_outcomes.stan"

# Compile Stan model 2
three_outcome_initial <- cmdstan_model(stan_file)

three_outcome_initial_fitted <- three_outcome_initial$sample(
  data = stan_data,
  seed = 42
)
```
### Extract the fitted ratings and draw tendencies
```{r}
rating_names <- paste0("rating[", seq_along(engines), "]")

posterior_draws <- as.matrix(three_outcome_initial_fitted$draws(
  variables = c(rating_names, "draw_tendency"),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

ratings <- posterior_draws[, rating_names, drop = FALSE]
draw_tendency <- posterior_draws[, "draw_tendency"]
```


### Simulate Tournament
```{r}


outcome_rep <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ratings)), function(s) {
  white_rating <- ratings[s, stan_data$white]
  black_rating <- ratings[s, stan_data$black]

  e <- 1 / (1 + 10^((black_rating - white_rating) / 400))

  p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency[s] * e * (1 - e)
  p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

  u <- runif(stan_data$N)

  ifelse(u < p_white, 1L,
         ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L))
}, FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data$N))
```

### Compare
```{r}
observed_draws <- sum(stan_data$outcome == 2L)
simulated_draws <- colSums(outcome_rep == 2L)

hist(
  simulated_draws,
  main = "Posterior predictive check: total draws",
  xlab = "Number of draws per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(simulated_draws, observed_draws))
)
abline(v = observed_draws, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_draws
quantile(simulated_draws, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```
The observed count of 80 draws in the actual tournament lies near the center of the posterior predictive distribution, so the model reproduces the overall number of draws reasonably well.

```{r}
observed <- stan_data$outcome

observed_score <- (observed == 1L) + 0.5 * (observed == 2L)
simulated_score <- (outcome_rep == 1L) + 0.5 * (outcome_rep == 2L)

observed_draw <- observed == 2L
simulated_draw <- outcome_rep == 2L
```


```{r}
observed_white_wins <- sum(observed == 1L)
replicated_white_wins <- colSums(outcome_rep == 1L)

observed_white_wins
quantile(replicated_white_wins, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```
Here we clearely see that the model underpredicts the win probability for white, we can therefore try to inprove the model by adding another parameter.

### Model adjustment: White advantage
Based on the discrepencies above i suggest and will now try a scalar white advantage parameter that is equal for every model.

$$e_n = \frac{1}{1 + 10^{(\Delta_n)/400}}$$
where $\Delta_n$ is now defined as:

$$\Delta_n = R_{\text{Black},n} - (R_{\text{White},n} + \text{whiteAdvantage})$$

### New model after iteration 1
```{r}
stan_file_1 <- "helpers/rating_three_outcomes_first_iteration.stan"

# Compile Stan model 2
three_outcome_iteration_1 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file_1)

three_outcome_iteration_1_fitted <- three_outcome_iteration_1$sample(
  data = stan_data,
  seed = 42
)
```

### Extract the fitted ratings and draw tendencies
```{r}
rating_names <- paste0("rating[", seq_along(engines), "]")

posterior_draws_1 <- as.matrix(three_outcome_iteration_1_fitted$draws(
  variables = c(rating_names, "draw_tendency", "white_advantage"),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

ratings <- posterior_draws_1[, rating_names, drop = FALSE]
draw_tendency <- posterior_draws_1[, "draw_tendency"]
white_advantage <- posterior_draws_1[, "white_advantage"]
```

### Simulate Tournament
```{r}


outcome_rep <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ratings)), function(s) {
  white_rating <- ratings[s, stan_data$white]
  black_rating <- ratings[s, stan_data$black]
  
  e <- 1 / (1 + 10^((black_rating - (white_rating + white_advantage[s])) / 400))

  p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency[s] * e * (1 - e)
  p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

  u <- runif(stan_data$N)

  ifelse(u < p_white, 1L,
         ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L))
}, FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data$N))
```

### Compare
```{r}
observed_draws <- sum(stan_data$outcome == 2L)
simulated_draws <- colSums(outcome_rep == 2L)

hist(
  simulated_draws,
  main = "Posterior predictive check: total draws",
  xlab = "Number of draws per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(simulated_draws, observed_draws))
)
abline(v = observed_draws, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_draws
quantile(simulated_draws, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```
This stayed unchanged and the model satisfies the posterior check.
```{r}
observed <- stan_data$outcome

observed_score <- (observed == 1L) + 0.5 * (observed == 2L)
simulated_score <- (outcome_rep == 1L) + 0.5 * (outcome_rep == 2L)

observed_draw <- observed == 2L
simulated_draw <- outcome_rep == 2L
```


```{r}
observed_white_wins <- sum(observed == 1L)
replicated_white_wins <- colSums(outcome_rep == 1L)

observed_white_wins
quantile(replicated_white_wins, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```
Now the median of the posterior distribution matches the amount of white wins from the actual tournament pretty exactly.

As both draws and white wins are satisfactory we do not need to look into the black win rate.

### Win and draws by matchup
We now look at specific matchups between different engines and look if the posterior distribution reasonably matches with the observed tournament data
```{r, helper_function}
check_by_group <- function(group, observed_values, simulated_values) {
  groups <- split(seq_along(observed_values), group)

  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(groups), function(label) {
    rows <- groups[[label]]

    observed_mean <- mean(observed_values[rows])
    replicated_means <- colMeans(
      simulated_values[rows, , drop = FALSE]
    )

    q <- quantile(replicated_means, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))

    data.frame(
      Group = label,
      Games = length(rows),
      Observed = observed_mean,
      Predicted_median = q[[2]],
      Lower_90 = q[[1]],
      Upper_90 = q[[3]]
    )
  }))
}
```

```{r}
matchup <- paste(games$white, "vs", games$black)

draws_by_matchup <- check_by_group(
  matchup,
  stan_data$outcome == 2L,
  outcome_rep == 2L
)

white_wins_by_matchup <- check_by_group(
  matchup,
  stan_data$outcome == 1L,
  outcome_rep == 1L
)

scores_by_matchup <- check_by_group(
  matchup,
  (stan_data$outcome == 1L) + 0.5 * (stan_data$outcome == 2L),
  (outcome_rep == 1L) + 0.5 * (outcome_rep == 2L)
)



knitr::kable(draws_by_matchup, digits = 3)

```

In the first table we can observe that the model underpredicts draws for D playing White against E and overpredicts draws for E playing White against SM. This can be overlooked if we only look at the total number of draws in the whole tournament. 

```{r}
knitr::kable(white_wins_by_matchup, digits = 3)

```
SM as white vs A has the largest gap from the predictive median. SM won 7 of 28 games in the actual tournament, but the model predicted a median of 14 wins.

```{r}
knitr::kable(scores_by_matchup, digits = 3)
```
In here we look at the scores per matchup and can see that a total of five matchup scores lie outside their 90% posterior predictive intervals. The model underpredicts D’s score against E and E’s score against A, while overpredicting D’s score against SM and a few others. These discrepancies combined with the ones analyzed above clearely indicate that the model is yet not good enough in predicting oucomes reliably for specific matchups. 

### Model revision: matchup-specific adjustment

We extend the model with an Elo adjustment for each unordered engine pair. The adjustment changes sign when the colors reverse, allowing an engine to perform better against a particular opponent in either color.

For game \(n\), we define

$$
\Delta_n = R_{\text{Black},n} - (R_{\text{White},n} + \text{whiteAdvantage} + \text{matchupDirection} \cdot \text{paireff}_{p(n)}),
$$
$$
e_n = \frac{1}{1 + 10^{\Delta_n/400}},
$$

where , $p(n)$ identifies the engine pair, and matchup direction is $+1$ when White has the smaller engine
ID and $-1$ otherwise.

To model paireff we use a hierarchical prior

$$
\text{pair}_{raw} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)
$$
$$
\text{matchup}_{sd} \sim \operatorname{HalfNormal}(0,50)
$$

$$
\text{parieff} = \text{matchup}_{sd} \cdot \text{pair}_{raw}.
$$
where $\text{pair}_{raw}$ is modeled for every unorderd pair and $\text{matchup}_{sd}$ is modeled over all games and all matchups. The shared scale allows the data to inform the amount of matchup variation while shrinking weakly supported effects toward zero. We retain the existing draw model and repeat the posterior predictive checks to assess the new model.


### Data preperation
```{r}
stan_data_pairs <- stan_data

# All unordered engine pairs
pairs <- combn(seq_along(engines), 2)
P <- ncol(pairs)

pair_lookup <- matrix(0L, length(engines), length(engines))

for (p in seq_len(P)) {
  i <- pairs[1, p]
  j <- pairs[2, p]

  pair_lookup[i, j] <- p
  pair_lookup[j, i] <- p
}

stan_data_pairs$P <- P

stan_data_pairs$pair_id <- pair_lookup[
  cbind(stan_data$white, stan_data$black)
]

# Positive effects favor the engine with the smaller ID
stan_data_pairs$matchup_direction <- ifelse(
  stan_data$white < stan_data$black, 1L, -1L
)

stopifnot(all(stan_data_pairs$pair_id >= 1L))

# Labels for interpreting the fitted effects
pair_labels <- paste(
  engines[pairs[1, ]],
  "vs",
  engines[pairs[2, ]]
)
```


### Fit model

```{r}
mod_pairs <- cmdstan_model("helpers/rating_three_outcomes_second_iteration.stan")

fit_pairs <- mod_pairs$sample(
  data = stan_data_pairs,
  seed = 42
)

fit_pairs$summary(
  variables = c("white_advantage", "matchup_sd", "pair_effect")
)

fit_pairs$diagnostic_summary()
```



### Simulate Tournament

```{r}
rating_names <- paste0("rating[", seq_along(engines), "]")
pair_names <- paste0("pair_effect[", seq_len(P), "]")

posterior_pairs <- as.matrix(fit_pairs$draws(
  variables = c(
    rating_names, pair_names,
    "draw_tendency", "white_advantage"
  ),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

ratings_pairs <- posterior_pairs[, rating_names, drop = FALSE]
effects_pairs <- posterior_pairs[, pair_names, drop = FALSE]

set.seed(42)

outcome_rep_pairs <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(posterior_pairs)), function(s) {
  white_rating <- as.numeric(ratings_pairs[s, stan_data_pairs$white])
  black_rating <- as.numeric(ratings_pairs[s, stan_data_pairs$black])

  adjustment <- as.numeric(stan_data_pairs$matchup_direction) *
    as.numeric(effects_pairs[s, stan_data_pairs$pair_id])
  
  delta <- black_rating - (white_rating + 
    as.numeric(posterior_pairs[s, "white_advantage"]) + adjustment)

  e <- 1 / (1 + 10^(delta / 400))

  p_draw <- 2 * posterior_pairs[s, "draw_tendency"] * e * (1 - e)
  p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

  u <- runif(stan_data_pairs$N)

  ifelse(u < p_white, 1L,
         ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L))
}, FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data_pairs$N))
```

### Prepare the observed and simulated statistics
```{r}
observed_pairs <- stan_data_pairs$outcome

observed_draw_pairs <- observed_pairs == 2L
simulated_draw_pairs <- outcome_rep_pairs == 2L

observed_white_win_pairs <- observed_pairs == 1L
simulated_white_win_pairs <- outcome_rep_pairs == 1L

observed_score_pairs <- (observed_pairs == 1L) +
  0.5 * (observed_pairs == 2L)

simulated_score_pairs <- (outcome_rep_pairs == 1L) +
  0.5 * (outcome_rep_pairs == 2L)
```

### Overall draw count, including the histogram
```{r}
observed_draws_pairs <- sum(observed_draw_pairs)
simulated_draws_pairs <- colSums(simulated_draw_pairs)

hist(
  simulated_draws_pairs,
  main = "Matchup model: total draws",
  xlab = "Number of draws per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(simulated_draws_pairs, observed_draws_pairs))
)

abline(v = observed_draws_pairs, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_draws_pairs
quantile(simulated_draws_pairs, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

### Overall White-win count
```{r}
observed_white_wins_pairs <- sum(observed_white_win_pairs)
replicated_white_wins_pairs <- colSums(simulated_white_win_pairs)

hist(
  replicated_white_wins_pairs,
  main = "Matchup model: total White wins",
  xlab = "Number of White wins per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(
    replicated_white_wins_pairs,
    observed_white_wins_pairs
  ))
)

abline(v = observed_white_wins_pairs, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_white_wins_pairs
quantile(replicated_white_wins_pairs, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

### Overall White mean score
```{r}
observed_white_score_pairs <- mean(observed_score_pairs)
replicated_white_scores_pairs <- colMeans(simulated_score_pairs)

observed_white_score_pairs
quantile(replicated_white_scores_pairs, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

### Draw rates by matchup
```{r}
matchup_pairs <- paste(games$white, "vs", games$black)

draws_by_matchup_pairs <- check_by_group(
  matchup_pairs,
  observed_draw_pairs,
  simulated_draw_pairs
)

knitr::kable(
  draws_by_matchup_pairs,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Matchup model: draw rate by matchup"
)
```
We can still observe some discrepencies in the amount of draws predicted in some matchups. We will adress this in the next model iteration.

### White win rate by matchup
```{r}
white_wins_by_matchup_pairs <- check_by_group(
  matchup_pairs,
  observed_white_win_pairs,
  simulated_white_win_pairs
)

knitr::kable(
  white_wins_by_matchup_pairs,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Matchup model: White win rate by matchup"
)
```
This overall looks fine now with some deviation for E vs A but it lies within the 90% range.

### White’s mean score by matchup
```{r}
scores_by_matchup_pairs <- check_by_group(
  matchup_pairs,
  observed_score_pairs,
  simulated_score_pairs
)

knitr::kable(
  scores_by_matchup_pairs,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Matchup model: White's mean score by matchup"
)
```

All checks are passed with minor deviation, except for the drawrate. We experience a similar phenomenon as with the win and score. For certain matchups the ammount of draws lies outside the 90% interval. We will therefore also use a similar approach in fixing it by using drawrates for every matchup.

### Model revision: Draw rate adjustment per matchup

We therefore allow each unordered engine pair to have its own draw tendency, shared across both color arrangements.


$$
\text{matchupDrawAdjustment} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1),
\qquad
\text{adjustedDrawTendency} = \operatorname{logit}^{-1} \left(\operatorname{logit}(\text{drawTendency})+\text{matchup DrawAdjustment}\right),
$$

Because we want the adjusted draw tendency to be in $[0, 1]$ we first use  logit before adding the adjustment and then converting to the interval using the inverse logit again. We then use this adjusted draw tendency the same way as before.


### Fit the revised model
```{r}
mod_pair_draws <- cmdstan_model(
  "helpers/rating_three_outcomes_third_iteration.stan"
)

fit_pair_draws <- mod_pair_draws$sample(
  data = stan_data_pairs,
  seed = 42
)
```


### Inspect sampling diagnostics
```{r}
summary_pair_draws <- fit_pair_draws$summary(
  variables = c(
    "rating",
    "white_advantage",
    "matchup_sd",
    "draw_tendency",
    "pair_effect",
    "draw_adjustment",
    "adjusted_draw_tendency"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_pair_draws[, c(
    "variable", "mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
  )],
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Pair-specific draw model: posterior summary"
)

fit_pair_draws$diagnostic_summary()
```


### Extract the posterior draws

```{r}
rating_names <- paste0(
  "rating[", seq_along(engines), "]"
)

pair_names <- paste0(
  "pair_effect[", seq_len(stan_data_pairs$P), "]"
)

draw_tendency_names <- paste0(
  "adjusted_draw_tendency[",
  seq_len(stan_data_pairs$P),
  "]"
)

posterior_pair_draws <- as.matrix(fit_pair_draws$draws(
  variables = c(
    rating_names,
    pair_names,
    draw_tendency_names,
    "white_advantage"
  ),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

ratings_pair_draws <- posterior_pair_draws[
  , rating_names, drop = FALSE
]

effects_pair_draws <- posterior_pair_draws[
  , pair_names, drop = FALSE
]

tendencies_pair_draws <- posterior_pair_draws[
  , draw_tendency_names, drop = FALSE
]
```

### Simulate the tournaments

```{r}
set.seed(42)

outcome_rep_pair_draws <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(posterior_pair_draws)),
  function(s) {

    white_rating <- as.numeric(
      ratings_pair_draws[s, stan_data_pairs$white]
    )

    black_rating <- as.numeric(
      ratings_pair_draws[s, stan_data_pairs$black]
    )

    white_advantage_s <- as.numeric(
      posterior_pair_draws[s, "white_advantage"]
    )

    adjustment <- as.numeric(
      stan_data_pairs$matchup_direction
    ) * as.numeric(
      effects_pair_draws[s, stan_data_pairs$pair_id]
    )

    # Select the draw tendency for each game's engine pair
    draw_tendency_game <- as.numeric(
      tendencies_pair_draws[s, stan_data_pairs$pair_id]
    )

    stopifnot(
      length(white_rating) == stan_data_pairs$N,
      length(black_rating) == stan_data_pairs$N,
      length(adjustment) == stan_data_pairs$N,
      length(draw_tendency_game) == stan_data_pairs$N
    )

    delta <- black_rating -
      (white_rating + white_advantage_s + adjustment)

    e <- 1 / (1 + 10^(delta / 400))

    p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency_game * e * (1 - e)
    p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

    u <- runif(stan_data_pairs$N)

    ifelse(
      u < p_white,
      1L,
      ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L)
    )
  },
  FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data_pairs$N)
)
```
Each column of outcome_rep_pair_draws is one simulated tournament. Each row corresponds to the same game as in games and stan_data_pairs.

### Prepare all checking statistics

```{r}
observed_pair_draws <- stan_data_pairs$outcome

observed_draw_pair_draws <- observed_pair_draws == 2L
simulated_draw_pair_draws <- outcome_rep_pair_draws == 2L

observed_white_win_pair_draws <- observed_pair_draws == 1L
simulated_white_win_pair_draws <- outcome_rep_pair_draws == 1L

observed_black_win_pair_draws <- observed_pair_draws == 3L
simulated_black_win_pair_draws <- outcome_rep_pair_draws == 3L

observed_score_pair_draws <-
  as.numeric(observed_white_win_pair_draws) +
  0.5 * observed_draw_pair_draws

simulated_score_pair_draws <-
  simulated_white_win_pair_draws +
  0.5 * simulated_draw_pair_draws
```

```{r}
observed_draws_pair_draws <- sum(observed_draw_pair_draws)
replicated_draws_pair_draws <- colSums(simulated_draw_pair_draws)

hist(

  main = "Pair-specific draw model: total draws",

  xlim = range(c(
    replicated_draws_pair_draws,
    observed_draws_pair_draws
  ))
)

abline(v = observed_draws_pair_draws, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_draws_pair_draws
quantile(replicated_draws_pair_draws, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

### Overall Black-win count and White’s mean score
```{r}
# Black wins
observed_black_wins_pair_draws <-
  sum(observed_black_win_pair_draws)
```

Pair specific draw tendencies improve the reproduction of our matchup draw rates. All observed White win rates and mean scores lie within their displayed 90% posterior predictive intervals. One draw-rate discrepancy remains for C playing White against A, where all three games were draws. Given the small sample, we acknowledge but ignore this small error.
I therefore concider this part of the optimization complete for the non time control model.

```{r}

```
## Time controll model

### Data Preparation for Stan

```{r}
# Engine identifiers
engines <- sort(unique(c(games$white, games$black)))

# Convert time controls into expected game duration
parts <- strsplit(games$timecontrol, "\\+")

tc <- vapply(parts, function(p) {
  as.numeric(p[1]) + 40 * as.numeric(p[2])
}, numeric(1))

# Standardize time control
tc_center <- mean(tc)
tc_scale <- sd(tc)
stopifnot(is.finite(tc_scale), tc_scale > 0)

x <- (tc - tc_center) / tc_scale

# Encode the three game outcomes
outcome_levels <- c("1-0", "1/2-1/2", "0-1")

# Data for the time-control model
stan_data_tc <- list(
  N = nrow(games),
  K = length(engines),
  white = match(games$white, engines),
  black = match(games$black, engines),
  outcome = match(games$result, outcome_levels),
  x = as.numeric(x)
)
```

### Posterior Sampling

```{r}
# Compile time-control model
mod_tc <- cmdstan_model("helpers/rating_timecontrol.stan")

# Sample from the posterior
fit_tc <- mod_tc$sample(
  data = stan_data_tc,
  seed = 42
)
```
### Replicate tournament
```{r}
# Extract posterior draws from the time-control model
intercept_names <- paste0("intercept[", seq_along(engines), "]")
slope_names <- paste0("slope[", seq_along(engines), "]")

posterior_tc <- as.matrix(fit_tc$draws(
  variables = c(intercept_names, slope_names, "draw_tendency"),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

intercepts_tc <- posterior_tc[, intercept_names, drop = FALSE]
slopes_tc <- posterior_tc[, slope_names, drop = FALSE]
draw_tendency_tc <- posterior_tc[, "draw_tendency"]

# One simulated tournament per posterior draw
set.seed(42)

outcome_rep_tc <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(posterior_tc)), function(s) {

  # Use each game's standardized time control from the fitted data
  white_rating <- intercepts_tc[s, stan_data_tc$white] +
    slopes_tc[s, stan_data_tc$white] * stan_data_tc$x

  black_rating <- intercepts_tc[s, stan_data_tc$black] +
    slopes_tc[s, stan_data_tc$black] * stan_data_tc$x

  # Same probabilities as in rating_timecontrol.stan
  e <- plogis(log(10) / 400 * (white_rating - black_rating))

  p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency_tc[s] * e * (1 - e)
  p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

  u <- runif(stan_data_tc$N)

  ifelse(u < p_white, 1L,
         ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L))

}, FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data_tc$N))

# Observed and simulated statistics for the time-control model
observed_tc <- stan_data_tc$outcome

observed_draw_tc <- observed_tc == 2L
simulated_draw_tc <- outcome_rep_tc == 2L

observed_score_tc <- (observed_tc == 1L) + 0.5 * (observed_tc == 2L)

simulated_score_tc <- (outcome_rep_tc == 1L) + 0.5 * (outcome_rep_tc == 2L)
```

### Time controll analysis

```{r}
# Total draws
sum(observed_draw_tc)
quantile(
  colSums(simulated_draw_tc),
  c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
)

# Total White wins
sum(observed_tc == 1L)
quantile(
  colSums(outcome_rep_tc == 1L),
  c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
)

# White's mean score
mean(observed_score_tc)
quantile(
  colMeans(simulated_score_tc),
  c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
)
```

```{r}
matchup <- paste(games$white, "vs", games$black)

draws_by_tc <- check_by_group(
  games$timecontrol, observed_draw_tc, simulated_draw_tc
)

scores_by_tc <- check_by_group(
  games$timecontrol, observed_score_tc, simulated_score_tc
)

draws_by_matchup_tc <- check_by_group(
  matchup, observed_draw_tc, simulated_draw_tc
)

scores_by_matchup_tc <- check_by_group(
  matchup, observed_score_tc, simulated_score_tc
)

knitr::kable(
  draws_by_tc, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control model: draw rate by time control"
)

knitr::kable(
  scores_by_tc, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control model: White's mean score by time control"
)

knitr::kable(
  draws_by_matchup_tc, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control model: draw rate by matchup"
)

knitr::kable(
  scores_by_matchup_tc, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control model: White's mean score by matchup"
)
```
### Model adjustment: White advantage
In the same fashion as in the non timecontrol model we now add a constant white advantage for all to adress the underprediction of whit wins.

### Fit the revised model
```{r}
mod_tc_1 <- cmdstan_model(
  "helpers/rating_timecontrol_first_iteration.stan"
)

fit_tc_1 <- mod_tc_1$sample(
  data = stan_data_tc,
  seed = 42
)

fit_tc_1$diagnostic_summary()

fit_tc_1$summary(
  variables = c("white_advantage", "draw_tendency")
)
```


### Extract posterior draws

```{r}
intercept_names <- paste0(
  "intercept[", seq_along(engines), "]"
)

slope_names <- paste0(
  "slope[", seq_along(engines), "]"
)

posterior_tc_1 <- as.matrix(fit_tc_1$draws(
  variables = c(
    intercept_names,
    slope_names,
    "draw_tendency",
    "white_advantage"
  ),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

intercepts_tc_1 <- posterior_tc_1[
  , intercept_names, drop = FALSE
]

slopes_tc_1 <- posterior_tc_1[
  , slope_names, drop = FALSE
]
```

### Simulate tournaments
```{r}

set.seed(42)

outcome_rep_tc_1 <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(posterior_tc_1)),
  function(s) {

    white_rating <- as.numeric(
      intercepts_tc_1[s, stan_data_tc$white]
    ) + as.numeric(
      slopes_tc_1[s, stan_data_tc$white]
    ) * as.numeric(stan_data_tc$x)

    black_rating <- as.numeric(
      intercepts_tc_1[s, stan_data_tc$black]
    ) + as.numeric(
      slopes_tc_1[s, stan_data_tc$black]
    ) * as.numeric(stan_data_tc$x)

    white_advantage_s <- as.numeric(
      posterior_tc_1[s, "white_advantage"]
    )

    draw_tendency_s <- as.numeric(
      posterior_tc_1[s, "draw_tendency"]
    )

    e <- 1 / (1 + 10^(
      (black_rating - (white_rating + white_advantage_s)) / 400
    ))

    p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency_s * e * (1 - e)
    p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

    u <- runif(stan_data_tc$N)

    ifelse(
      u < p_white,
      1L,
      ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L)
    )
  },
  FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data_tc$N)
)
```

### Check the overall White-win count
```{r}

replicated_white_wins_tc_1 <- colSums(outcome_rep_tc_1 == 1L)

hist(
  replicated_white_wins_tc_1,
  main = "Time-control model with White advantage: White wins",
  xlab = "White wins per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(
    replicated_white_wins_tc_1,
    observed_white_wins_tc_1
  ))
)

abline(v = observed_white_wins_tc_1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_white_wins_tc_1
quantile(replicated_white_wins_tc_1, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))

```

```{r}
replicated_draws_tc_1 <- colSums(outcome_rep_tc_1 == 2L)

hist(
  replicated_draws_tc_1,
  main = "Time-control model with White advantage: draws",
  xlab = "Draws per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(
    replicated_draws_tc_1,
    observed_draws_tc_1
  ))
)

observed_draws_tc_1
quantile(replicated_draws_tc_1, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

### Check White’s overall mean score
```{r}

  (stan_data_tc$outcome == 1L) +
  0.5 * (stan_data_tc$outcome == 2L)

replicated_scores_tc_1 <-
  (outcome_rep_tc_1 == 1L) +
  0.5 * (outcome_rep_tc_1 == 2L)

mean(observed_scores_tc_1)
quantile(
  colMeans(replicated_scores_tc_1),
  c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
```

Now we were able to fix the white win count discrepency as in the non time control model.

We now take our attention to the draw, win and score distribution by matchup and timcontrol.

```{r}

simulated_draw_tc_1 <- outcome_rep_tc_1 == 2L

  0.5 * (stan_data_tc$outcome == 2L)

  0.5 * (outcome_rep_tc_1 == 2L)

  games$timecontrol, observed_score_tc_1, simulated_score_tc_1
```

Adding White advantage improves the reproduction of scores across time controls: all observed group mean scores lie within their displayed 90% posterior predictive intervals. However, several matchup score and draw-rate discrepancies persist. We therefore investigate pair-specific Elo adjustments as the next model revision, again analogous to the approach above.

### Add our existing pair information to the time-control data

We already created stan_data_pairs. So we reuse its mapping after verifying that the games and engine IDs align.

```{r}
stopifnot(
  stan_data_tc$K == stan_data_pairs$K,
  identical(stan_data_tc$white, stan_data_pairs$white),
  identical(stan_data_tc$black, stan_data_pairs$black),
  identical(stan_data_tc$outcome, stan_data_pairs$outcome)
)

stan_data_tc_2 <- stan_data_tc

stan_data_tc_2$P <- stan_data_pairs$P
stan_data_tc_2$pair_id <- stan_data_pairs$pair_id
stan_data_tc_2$matchup_direction <-
  stan_data_pairs$matchup_direction
```

### Extract draws and simulate tournaments
```{r}

outcome_rep_tc_2 <- vapply(

  function(s) {

    white_rating <- as.numeric(
      intercepts_tc_2[s, stan_data_tc_2$white]

    ) * as.numeric(stan_data_tc_2$x)

      intercepts_tc_2[s, stan_data_tc_2$black]
    ) + as.numeric(
      slopes_tc_2[s, stan_data_tc_2$black]
    ) * as.numeric(stan_data_tc_2$x)

    adjustment <- as.numeric(
      stan_data_tc_2$matchup_direction
    ) * as.numeric(

    )

    white_advantage_s <- as.numeric(
      posterior_tc_2[s, "white_advantage"]
    )

    draw_tendency_s <- as.numeric(
      posterior_tc_2[s, "draw_tendency"]
    )

    delta <- black_rating -
      (white_rating + white_advantage_s + adjustment)

    e <- 1 / (1 + 10^(delta / 400))

    p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency_s * e * (1 - e)
    p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

    u <- runif(stan_data_tc_2$N)

    ifelse(

      ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L)
```

### Model adjustment: Pair specific draw rate adjustment


### Compile and fit
```{r}
mod_tc_3 <- cmdstan_model(
  "helpers/rating_timecontrol_third_iteration.stan"
)

fit_tc_3 <- mod_tc_3$sample(
  data = stan_data_tc_2,
  seed = 42
)
```
### Check sampling diagnostics

```{r}
fit_tc_3$diagnostic_summary()

summary_tc_3 <- fit_tc_3$summary(
  variables = c(
    "intercept", "slope",
    "white_advantage", "matchup_sd",
    "pair_effect", "draw_tendency",
    "draw_adjustment", "adjusted_draw_tendency"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_tc_3[, c(
    "variable", "mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
  )],
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control iteration 3: posterior summary"
)
```
###Extract posterior draws

```{r}
intercept_names <- paste0(
  "intercept[", seq_along(engines), "]"
)

slope_names <- paste0(
  "slope[", seq_along(engines), "]"
)

pair_names <- paste0(
  "pair_effect[", seq_len(stan_data_tc_2$P), "]"
)

draw_names <- paste0(
  "adjusted_draw_tendency[", seq_len(stan_data_tc_2$P), "]"
)

posterior_tc_3 <- as.matrix(fit_tc_3$draws(
  variables = c(
    intercept_names, slope_names, pair_names,
    draw_names, "white_advantage"
  ),
  format = "draws_matrix"
))

intercepts_tc_3 <- posterior_tc_3[
  , intercept_names, drop = FALSE
]

slopes_tc_3 <- posterior_tc_3[
  , slope_names, drop = FALSE
]

effects_tc_3 <- posterior_tc_3[
  , pair_names, drop = FALSE
]

draw_tendencies_tc_3 <- posterior_tc_3[
  , draw_names, drop = FALSE
]
```
### Simulate tournaments
```{r}
set.seed(42)

outcome_rep_tc_3 <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(posterior_tc_3)),
  function(s) {

    white_rating <- as.numeric(
      intercepts_tc_3[s, stan_data_tc_2$white]
    ) + as.numeric(
      slopes_tc_3[s, stan_data_tc_2$white]
    ) * as.numeric(stan_data_tc_2$x)

    black_rating <- as.numeric(
      intercepts_tc_3[s, stan_data_tc_2$black]
    ) + as.numeric(
      slopes_tc_3[s, stan_data_tc_2$black]
    ) * as.numeric(stan_data_tc_2$x)

    adjustment <- as.numeric(
      stan_data_tc_2$matchup_direction
    ) * as.numeric(
      effects_tc_3[s, stan_data_tc_2$pair_id]
    )

    white_advantage_s <- as.numeric(
      posterior_tc_3[s, "white_advantage"]
    )

    draw_tendency_game <- as.numeric(
      draw_tendencies_tc_3[s, stan_data_tc_2$pair_id]
    )

    stopifnot(
      length(adjustment) == stan_data_tc_2$N,
      length(draw_tendency_game) == stan_data_tc_2$N
    )

    delta <- black_rating -
      (white_rating + white_advantage_s + adjustment)

    e <- 1 / (1 + 10^(delta / 400))

    p_draw <- 2 * draw_tendency_game * e * (1 - e)
    p_white <- e - 0.5 * p_draw

    u <- runif(stan_data_tc_2$N)

    ifelse(
      u < p_white,
      1L,
      ifelse(u < p_white + p_draw, 2L, 3L)
    )
  },
  FUN.VALUE = integer(stan_data_tc_2$N)
)
```

### Prepare checking statistics
```{r}

observed_draw_tc_3 <- observed_tc_3 == 2L
simulated_draw_tc_3 <- outcome_rep_tc_3 == 2L

observed_white_win_tc_3 <- observed_tc_3 == 1L
simulated_white_win_tc_3 <- outcome_rep_tc_3 == 1L

observed_score_tc_3 <- (observed_tc_3 == 1L) +
  0.5 * (observed_tc_3 == 2L)

simulated_score_tc_3 <- (outcome_rep_tc_3 == 1L) +
  0.5 * (outcome_rep_tc_3 == 2L)
```

### Overall draw count

```{r}

  replicated_draws_tc_3,
  main = "Time-control iteration 3: total draws",
  xlab = "Draws per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(replicated_draws_tc_3, observed_draws_tc_3))
)

abline(v = observed_draws_tc_3, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_draws_tc_3
quantile(replicated_draws_tc_3, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```
### Overall White-win count
```{r}
observed_white_wins_tc_3 <- sum(observed_white_win_tc_3)
replicated_white_wins_tc_3 <- colSums(simulated_white_win_tc_3)

hist(
  replicated_white_wins_tc_3,
  main = "Time-control iteration 3: total White wins",
  xlab = "White wins per replicated tournament",
  xlim = range(c(
    replicated_white_wins_tc_3,
    observed_white_wins_tc_3
  ))
)

abline(v = observed_white_wins_tc_3, col = "red", lwd = 2)

observed_white_wins_tc_3
quantile(replicated_white_wins_tc_3, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
```

### Overall Black-win count and White’s mean score
```{r}
# Black wins
observed_black_wins_tc_3 <- sum(observed_tc_3 == 3L)
replicated_black_wins_tc_3 <- colSums(outcome_rep_tc_3 == 3L)

observed_black_wins_tc_3
quantile(replicated_black_wins_tc_3, c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))

# White's mean score
mean(observed_score_tc_3)
quantile(
  colMeans(simulated_score_tc_3),
  c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
)
```

```{r}
matchup_tc_3 <- paste(games$white, "vs", games$black)

draws_by_matchup_tc_3 <- check_by_group(

  simulated_draw_tc_3
)

white_wins_by_matchup_tc_3 <- check_by_group(
  matchup_tc_3,
  observed_white_win_tc_3,
  simulated_white_win_tc_3
)

scores_by_matchup_tc_3 <- check_by_group(
  matchup_tc_3,
  observed_score_tc_3,
  simulated_score_tc_3
)

knitr::kable(
  draws_by_matchup_tc_3, digits = 3,
```

### Checks by time control
```{r}
draws_by_tc_3 <- check_by_group(
  games$timecontrol,
  observed_draw_tc_3,
  simulated_draw_tc_3
)

white_wins_by_tc_3 <- check_by_group(
  games$timecontrol,
  observed_white_win_tc_3,
  simulated_white_win_tc_3
)

scores_by_tc_3 <- check_by_group(
  games$timecontrol,
  observed_score_tc_3,
  simulated_score_tc_3
)

knitr::kable(
  draws_by_tc_3, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control iteration 3: draw rate by time control"
)

knitr::kable(
  white_wins_by_tc_3, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control iteration 3: White win rate by time control"
)

knitr::kable(
  scores_by_tc_3, digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-control iteration 3: White's mean score by time control"
)

```

Allowing pair-specific draw tendencies improves the reproduction of matchup draw rates. All displayed win-rate and mean-score observations lie within their respective 90% posterior predictive intervals as desired. Draw rates are also covered except for C playing White against A, but here only three games were played and all were draws. Some smaller differences remain, including overprediction of draws at 180+0. We acknowledge these smaller mispredictions but keep this model for now.
